sonnet.problem: The question asks the baker to guess the wording of a detail in the line (sea of glass, bronze or silver). Nothing on the earlier cards lets a baker reason it out. It is the same kind of question as the 'oil, myrrh or perfume' example.
sonnet.rule: **Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.**

sonnet.problem: This story card only repeats what choice card 6 just asked and answered: a Lamb who appeared to have been slain, standing at the throne. It adds no new moment to the passage.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card. / No recap cards.

sonnet.problem: Stop 1 card 7 already told that the seven torches of fire are 'the seven spirits of God'. This card asks the same fact again, and the earlier card gives away the answer.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact.

sonnet.problem: The story card says the Lamb 'comes to the One seated on the throne'. That tells the baker the Lamb acts for Himself, which gives away the False answer to the next card ('The Lamb waits for the mighty angel to hand Him the scroll').
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
